generateRandomMapDialog.oneZonePerPlayerPlus:
One zone per player plus a neutral zone between each pair, each
                                with its own biome/faction, roads connecting every zone, one
                                river, and biome-appropriate scenery. Player zones get a
                                faction-matched starting dwelling, mine, and guard; neutral
                                zones get a mine (guarded to its own real economic value) and
                                scaled treasure. No zone-shape variety yet.
generateRandomMapDialog.classicPickRichnessComplexityAnd: Classic: pick Richness, Complexity and Water below — everything else uses sensible defaults. Advanced: tune every slider yourself in the categories on the left. The two are never mixed: Classic ignores the Advanced sliders, and Advanced ignores the Classic selectors.
generateRandomMapDialog.howManyHeroesEachPlayer: How many heroes each player can have at once (the map's heroCountMax). Overrides the value of an imported game template.
generateRandomMapDialog.everyPlayerStartsWithA: Every player starts with a random faction, picked when the game starts, instead of one that matches the land around their start. The land is chosen freely too, so any player can start on any terrain.
generateRandomMapDialog.letsANeutralZoneHold: Lets a neutral zone hold one Pandora's Box, at a low chance (about 1 zone in 5). Off by default.
generateRandomMapDialog.theRightHalfOfThe: The right half of the map is an exact mirror image of the left half, so every player has precisely the same surroundings: the same zones, land, roads, mines, dwellings, guards and treasure. Players take turns on the two sides (player 1 on the left, player 2 on the right, player 3 on the left, ...), so two human players in the first two slots face each other and the AI players are split evenly. Needs an even number of players and an even map width. What differs: the starting heroes (each is unique), and everything is generated for the left half only, so mirrored maps have no rivers, islands or portals and no City Hold (there is no single city in the middle). Objects that straddle the middle line are left out. With random starting towns each player is still dealt their own random town.
generateRandomMapDialog.aGameTemplateIsA: A game template is a real Olden Era map-generator layout. Using one replaces this generator's own zone layout with the template's zones and connections (and its player count), and applies its per-zone settings: zone size, lake amount, guard strength, how rich each zone's content is, content limits, road types, and the template's game rules and bans. Terrain, objects and decoration are still generated by this tool.
generateRandomMapDialog.howTheZonesAreArranged: How the zones are arranged. Random picks one of the layouts for you. Layouts too crowded for this map size or with too many players are not offered.
generateRandomMapDialog.spellsNobodyCanLearnOr: Spells nobody can learn or cast on the generated map, picked per magic school. Added to any spells.banned in the RMG tuning file.
generateRandomMapDialog.artifactsThatWillNotAppear: Artifacts that will not appear on the generated map, picked by kind and slot. Written to the map's banned items.
generateRandomMapDialog.sameSeedSameMapThe: Same seed, same map. The number field for typing an exact seed lives in the Advanced category — this is the quick way to get a fresh random terrain result immediately.
generateRandomMapDialog.producesJustTheTileArrays: Produces just the tile arrays (biome/water/elevation) — no player spawners, no roads/rivers, no objects/guards/decoration. For a map maker who wants the random fractal terrain shape but places everything else themselves.
generateRandomMapDialog.previewTheTerrainAndUnless: Preview the terrain (and, unless Terrain only, roads/rivers) live before committing — tune sliders, watch the canvas update, then confirm each stage.
generateRandomMapDialog.0NoWaterAtAll: 0: no water at all. 1-50: Normal — lakes inside some neutral zones, amount scaling with the slider. 51-100: Islands — some neutral zones (and, per this generator's own default, every player's own zone) are fully cut off by water and reached only through a portal — Olden Era has no boats.
generateRandomMapDialog.independentFromTheWaterSlider: Independent from the Water slider (how MANY islands) — this controls how BIG each one is. Water side: mostly ocean, each island small (this mode's original look). Land side: mostly land, each island large, little open water.
generateRandomMapDialog.howMuchOfEachZones: How much of each zone's free area becomes raised (hill) or lowered (dry valley) terrain, and how likely a zone is to get either at all — both player and neutral zones are eligible (a player's own start tile itself always stays flat). Drives Hills and Valleys equally. Every hill/valley gets real ramp access.
generateRandomMapDialog.controlsThePenroseTilingZone: Controls the Penrose-tiling zone-shaping pass's own vertex density — low values give coarser, blockier zone/biome boundaries, high values give finer, more jagged ones.
generateRandomMapDialog.howTightlyZonesPackTogether: How tightly zones pack together. Below 1×: denser, more crowded zone interiors. Above 1×: more open space per zone, generally cleaner-looking roads.
generateRandomMapDialog.blendsTerrainBiomesOrganicallyAcross: Blends terrain biomes organically across zone borders (a real-data-calibrated Wave Function Collapse pass) instead of each zone's flat, sharply-edged biome fill — only tiles near a zone boundary are affected, zone interiors are unchanged. 0 = today's flat fill, no blending at all. Higher values widen the blended band and weaken each tile's bias toward its own zone's biome, so the max setting blends noticeably more than this feature's old on/off switch ever did.
generateRandomMapDialog.howMuchRoadsRiversCurve: How much roads/rivers curve. Low: mostly straight, broad sweeps if any. High: swings noticeably away from a straight line, with tighter, more frequent curves.
generateRandomMapDialog.theRoadsRiversPreviewsOwn: The roads/rivers preview's own randomness — independent from the terrain seed, so rerolling it never changes the terrain you already confirmed.
generateRandomMapDialog.howStronglyRealHandCrafted: How strongly real hand-crafted-map evidence steers placement: decoration thinning near roads (real density near a road ~0.78x the map's own average, rising to ~1.29x far from any road), decoration clustering by category (ponds cluster with ponds, mountains avoid ponds), decoration density by elevation/climb proximity (valley tiles ~3.19x denser, ramp-adjacent tiles ~0.66x as dense), and gold mines favoring Sand-biome zones (~2.02x more than Sand's own area share) — all four calibrated from the same real 18-map survey. 0 = today's flat, evidence-blind behavior for all four; higher looks progressively more like a hand-crafted map's own placement patterns.
generateRandomMapDialog.multiplierOnNeutralZoneTreasure: Multiplier on neutral-zone treasure-pile count, 0-3×. 1× is the generator's own default zone-size scaling, 3× (the max) triples it, 0 removes treasure piles entirely.
generateRandomMapDialog.chanceATreasureGuardSlot: Chance a treasure/guard slot places a real, specific object (a resource pile, a named artifact, a pre-composed army) instead of a random type.
generateRandomMapDialog.whichRealInteractableBuildingsSites: Which real interactable buildings/sites the RMG is allowed to pick from at all — every one is enabled by default.
generateRandomMapDialog.chanceARealMineDwelling: Chance a real mine/dwelling/resource/artifact gets an extra nearby guard, on top of its own zone's usual guard. Guards near a player's own starting city are kept easy/normal difficulty.
generateRandomMapDialog.wallsEveryZoneToZone: Walls every zone-to-zone boundary solid except at each connection's own road crossing, and places one guard at each of those gates — VCMI-style chokepoints, each at least Impossible difficulty. 'Strong'/'Very strong' scale that value up further.
generateRandomMapDialog.addsOneBonusPortalPair: Adds one bonus portal-pair shortcut between the map's two most distant zones, on top of the normal roads — a shortcut, not a replacement.
generateRandomMapDialog.tuneTerrainInTheSidebar: Tune terrain in the sidebar, then confirm to move on.
generateRandomMapDialog.tuneRoadRiverWindingIn: Tune road/river winding in the sidebar, then confirm. Final roads (and any water an object later needs to avoid) may shift slightly once the rest of the map generates.
generateRandomMapDialog.terrainAndRoadsRiversAre: Terrain and roads/rivers are confirmed. Adjust obstacles, treasure, guards, and everything else in the sidebar, then Generate.
generateRandomMapDialog.richnessInfo: How valuable the treasure is — from poor piles and cheap buildings to rich ones with powerful artifacts. Uses the game's own richness tiers.
generateRandomMapDialog.complexityInfo: How busy the map is — scales decoration, interactable objects, treasure piles and guard squads together.
generateRandomMapDialog.difficultyInfo: How strong the guard squads are and how fast they grow each week, using the game's own six difficulty levels. Neutral cities get guards at higher levels, and the map's lobby difficulty is set to match.
generateRandomMapDialog.waterInfo: How much water: none, a few to many lakes, or islands reached by portals.

ring.label: Ring
ring.description: Player and neutral zones alternate on one ring.
ring.details: One ring around the map: a player zone, a neutral zone, the next player zone, and so on, so there are as many neutral zones as players. Every zone touches only the two zones beside it. Each player has one neutral zone on either side, and a rival can only be reached by going through neutral zones around the ring.

ringCenter.label: Ring with center
ringCenter.description: The ring plus a treasure zone in the middle, reachable from every neutral zone.
ringCenter.details: The same ring of player and neutral zones as Ring, plus one large treasure zone in the middle of the map. Every neutral zone on the ring connects to the middle zone, which holds extra treasure, so there are shortcuts across the map. Player zones do not connect to the middle directly.

innerRing.label: Inner ring
innerRing.description: Players on the outside; the neutral zones form an inner ring of their own.
innerRing.details: Players sit at the edge of the map and the neutral zones form a smaller ring in the middle. Each player zone connects to the two inner zones nearest to it, and the inner zones connect to each other around the ring. Player zones never touch each other, so every route between players runs through the middle. Offered for up to 7 players.

doubleNeutral.label: Double neutral
doubleNeutral.description: Two neutral zones between neighbouring players.
doubleNeutral.details: A ring where each pair of neighbouring player zones has two neutral zones in a row between them (player, neutral, neutral, player, ...). Rivals are further apart and the map has twice as many neutral zones as players. Every zone touches only the two beside it. Offered for up to 4 players.

pockets.label: Pockets
pockets.description: An inner ring, plus a dead-end treasure pocket behind each neutral zone.
pockets.details: A tighter ring of player and neutral zones in the middle of the map, as in Ring. Behind each neutral zone, towards the map edge, lies a small dead-end treasure pocket with richer treasure that is reached only through that neutral zone. Offered for up to 4 players.

hub.label: Hub
hub.description: A spoke from every player to a shared center; no direct ring between players.
hub.details: Like the hub of a wheel: each player has a single neutral zone towards the middle, and all of these connect to one large central zone with extra treasure. There is no ring between players, so the only way to a rival is through your neutral zone and the centre. Offered for up to 4 players.

winConditionsPanel.whichWaysTheGeneratedMap: Which ways the generated map can be won. Several can be on at once; at least one stays on. Default is Classic only.

classic.label: Classic
classic.details: The normal rule: a player wins by eliminating every enemy player. It stays available alongside the others, so you can combine it with extra ways to win.

capital-hold.label: Capital Hold
capital-hold.description: Capture the opponent's starting city and hold it for a set number of in-game days to win.
capital-hold.details: Capture the opponent's starting city and hold it for a set number of in-game days to win. Set the number of days below.

city-hold.label: City Hold
city-hold.description: Capture the marked neutral city and hold it for a set number of in-game days to win.
city-hold.details: Capture the marked neutral city and hold it for a set number of in-game days to win. The generator marks one neutral city near the middle of the map. With no neutral city on the map this condition is dropped (turn on random cities).

guardians-demise.label: Guardian's Demise
guardians-demise.description: Defeat or cast away the opponent's main hero to win.
guardians-demise.details: Defeat or cast away the opponent's main hero to win. The game does not tell the player which opponent or hero this is, so it appears to be picked at random. It has no settings.

final-battle.label: Final Battle
final-battle.description: Face the opponent's hero in a final battle. The winner claims victory in the game.
final-battle.details: Face the opponent's hero in a final battle. The winner claims victory in the game. Set the battle date below.

tournament.label: Tournament
tournament.description: Face the opponent's hero in a series of battles. The winner of the set claims victory.
tournament.details: Face the opponent's hero in a series of battles. The winner of the set claims victory. The number of battles is always odd (best-of-1, 3, 5, ...), added two at a time.

artifactBonusesEditor.xToAllCreatureGrowth: +X% to all creature growth, in every city you own.

customArtifactEditorDialog.clickToChangeTheBase: Click to change the base artifact

customBuffEditorDialog.clonesARealBuffStatus: Clones a real buff/status-effect definition under a brand-new id, or builds one from scratch. A buff has no identity of its own on the map — grant it by referencing its id from an artifact bonus, object reward, or (once supported) a custom skill/spell.
customBuffEditorDialog.cloneOneBuffEveryField: Clone one buff: every field starts from a real buff's own values. Build from scratch: stats/tags start blank. Switchable at any time.
customBuffEditorDialog.theRealBuffWhoseDefinition: The real buff whose definition this custom buff clones. Everything except id/name/description/icon is copied verbatim.
customBuffEditorDialog.searchForABuffTo: Search for a buff to clone…

customBuffEditorDialog.buildingFromScratchStatsAnd: Building from scratch — stats and tags start blank below.
customBuffEditorDialog.clickToChangeTheBase: Click to change the base buff

customBuffEditorDialog.isAlreadyUsedByAnother: "{{trimmedId}}" is already used by another buff.

storyBuilderDialog.alwaysIncludedEnglish: English is always included. Added languages are translated drafts; check them before publishing.
storyBuilderDialog.alwaysIncludedBoth: {{language}} + English are always included. Added languages are translated drafts; check them before publishing.

textWriterSettingsDialog.optionalWithAFreeKey: Optional. With a free key, stories get richer text, can be written in other languages and can be built from your own idea. Without it, the built-in text is used.

textWriterSettingsDialog.iUnderstandThatTextWritten: I understand that text written here, and any story idea I type, is sent to {{label}} to be written. Free plans may use it to improve their models, so do not include anything private.

scenario.slideHasBothEndAnd: Slide has both "end" and "next" ("{{next}}") — the game would ignore one. Pick one.
scenario.slideHasNoNextNo: Slide has no "next", no "end", and no answers — the dialog stops here.
scenario.textSIDHasNoLocalization: Text SID "{{text}}" has no localization token.
scenario.speakerSIDHasNoLocalization: Speaker SID "{{titleSid}}" has no localization token — the dialog will show the raw SID.
scenario.positionIsOutsideThe1: Position {{position}} is outside the 1–5 range the game renders.
scenario.isForegroundShouldBeTheString: "isForeground" should be the string "true" or "false", not {{value}}.
scenario.answerTextSIDHasNo: Answer text SID "{{text}}" has no localization token.
scenario.answerHasNoFlowActions: Answer has no flow actions — it leads nowhere.
scenario.goActionHasNoTarget: "Go" action has no target slide ID.
scenario.noSlideEndsTheDialog: No slide ends the dialog — mark a slide as "end" or give an answer an "End" action.
scenario.mapNameIsEmptyIt: Map name is empty. It is required to export a ZIP with dialog files.
scenario.actionReferencesDialogKeyWhich: Action "{{a}}" references dialog key "{{key}}" which has no dialog flow defined.
scenario.questNameSIDHasNo: Quest name SID "{{name}}" has no localization token.
scenario.subQuestNameSIDHasNo: SubQuest name SID "{{name}}" has no localization token.
scenario.counterIsNotDefinedIn: {{a}}: counter "{{sid}}" is not defined in counters.
scenario.questIsNotDefinedIn: {{a}}: quest "{{questSid}}" is not defined in quests.

story.counterIsCheckedButNothing: Counter is checked but nothing ever changes it from 0, so that check can never succeed past 0.
story.counterIsChangedButNever: Counter is changed but never checked anywhere.
story.unprefixedDialogIds: {{count}} dialog id(s) do not start with "{{prefix}}" (e.g. {{sample}}). Dialog ids are shared by every map and zip in the game; a repeated id overwrites the other one.

map.blockedEntrance: {{where}} — entrance is fully blocked (can't be reached)
map.elevationSpike: {{sid}} (id {{id}}) at ({{x}}, {{z}}) sits on a level-{{fromLevel}} tile surrounded by level {{toLevel}}
map.unreachableSealedByElevation: {{where}} — unreachable from any player start: sealed by a raised/lowered terrain level with no ramp connecting it to the rest of the map. This can't be auto-fixed; add a climb ramp or adjust the terrain yourself.
map.unreachableSealed: {{where}} — unreachable from any player start (sealed by terrain/water, nothing placed to move)
map.unreachableBlockedBy: {{where}} — unreachable from any player start, blocked by: {{blockers}}
map.isolatedPlayerStart: Player {{owner}}'s {{sid}} (id {{id}}) at ({{x}}, {{z}}) can't reach any other player's start — no connected path or bridging portal. Whichever side has less of the map's real content is effectively unplayable for that player, even though findUnreachablePlacements won't flag any of it (it's still "reachable", just only by the other player).

balance.outsideArea: {{start}} is not inside any Player Area, so it is not compared. Paint an area over its start tile.
balance.sharedArea: {{starts}} share Player Area {{zone}}, so only one of them is compared. Give each start its own area.
balance.emptyArea: Player Area {{zone}} has no city or hero start inside it.
balance.reasonMines: Distance to the starting mines differs by {{pct}}%
balance.reasonSites: Number of sites to claim differs by {{pct}}%
balance.reasonTerrain: Hills/valleys around the starts differ by {{points}} points
balance.landLess: Player {{owner}} has {{pct}}% less land than the typical player ({{tiles}} vs {{median}} tiles): paint more of the surrounding ground as their Player Area, or turn some of their water or blocked ground into land.
balance.landMore: Player {{owner}} has {{pct}}% more land than the typical player ({{tiles}} vs {{median}} tiles): shrink their Player Area, or give the others more room.
balance.minesFar: Player {{owner}}'s mines are on average {{distance}} tiles from their start, the typical player's {{median}}: move one or two of their mines closer.
balance.minesNear: Player {{owner}}'s mines are only {{distance}} tiles from their start, the typical player's {{median}}: move one of their mines farther out, or bring the others' closer.
balance.sitesFew: Player {{owner}} has {{sites}} sites to claim, the typical player {{median}}: add a few mines, dwellings, resource piles or artifacts in their area.
balance.sitesMany: Player {{owner}} has {{sites}} sites to claim, the typical player {{median}}: remove a few from their area, or add some for the others.
balance.terrainMore: Player {{owner}}'s area is {{pct}}% hills or valleys against the typical player's {{median}}%: flatten some of it.
balance.terrainLess: Player {{owner}}'s area is only {{pct}}% hills or valleys against the typical player's {{median}}%: raise or lower some ground to match the others.

progress.populatingZones: Populating zones with mines, dwellings and cities
